name: Mission and operator profiling
description: Collect public material on what the mission does, who pays for it and who depends on it, to judge which effect would matter most.
precondition: Mission information is public through press, procurement, customer or academic channels.
detection: Rarely visible; exposure reviews and unusual interest in staff or documents are the practical signals.

assessment.question: Could an outsider name our most valuable service and its most dependent customer from public sources alone?
assessment.evidence: A target pack assembled by an independent reviewer within a fixed time box.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm the mission can state which public disclosures were accepted and which were withdrawn.

name: Regulatory filing harvest
description: Read spectrum, licensing and coordination filings to learn frequencies, emission types, orbits and station locations.
precondition: The mission has filed with national or international spectrum and licensing bodies.
detection: Not detectable; treat filed parameters as known to every adversary.

assessment.question: Which link and station parameters can be recovered from our filings, and does any protection rely on them being secret?
assessment.evidence: A table of parameters recovered from filings against those in the interface documents.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; verify no control assumes these values are confidential.

name: Orbit and pass prediction
description: Use published orbital elements to predict when the spacecraft is in view of a given location and when operators are in contact.
precondition: Orbital elements are published or can be derived from observation.
detection: Not detectable; correlate later radio events with predicted adversary visibility.

assessment.question: At which points in the orbit is the spacecraft in view of uncontrolled territory but out of our own contact?
assessment.evidence: A visibility timeline marking operator contact, out-of-contact periods and third-party visibility.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm out-of-contact autonomy is safe if commands arrive only from an untrusted source.

name: Spacecraft design intelligence gathering
description: Assemble design knowledge from papers, theses, vendor datasheets, manuals, conference talks and open-source flight software.
precondition: Design details have been published by the operator, its suppliers or academic partners.
detection: Download and access patterns on documentation portals; otherwise not detectable.

assessment.question: How complete a picture of the on-board architecture and command set can be built without any insider help?
assessment.evidence: An architecture sketch produced by a reviewer from public material, with sources.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; feed findings into the exposure register.

name: Ground station and teleport mapping
description: Locate antennas, teleports and service providers from imagery, filings, provider marketing and network data.
precondition: Stations are fixed, visible and often shared with other operators.
detection: Physical surveillance indicators at sites; scanning of station address space.

assessment.question: Which stations and providers carry our commands, and which of them could an outsider identify?
assessment.evidence: A list of sites and providers identified externally versus the real contact plan.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm an alternate site exists that does not appear in the same public sources.

name: Passive downlink signal survey
description: Receive and record the spacecraft's emissions to learn modulation, framing, beacons and operating habits.
precondition: A receiver within the downlink footprint; nothing more.
detection: Passive reception cannot be detected.

assessment.question: What can be learned about spacecraft state and operations from an unkeyed receiver in the footprint?
assessment.evidence: Decoded frame structure and any readable fields from a lab capture of the mission's own downlink.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm encrypted downlinks reveal no state through unprotected headers or beacons.

name: Command and telemetry format reconstruction
description: Rebuild the meaning of telemetry and command structures from captures, public decoders, leaked databases or shared standards.
precondition: Captured traffic, a published standard or a leaked or open command database.
detection: Leak monitoring for mission databases; otherwise not detectable.

assessment.question: If the command database leaked tomorrow, what would still stop a third party issuing a valid command?
assessment.evidence: A statement of which protections remain when formats are assumed known.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm no safety case depends on format obscurity.

name: Workforce and contractor research
description: Identify operators, engineers and suppliers, and infer tools and technologies from profiles, adverts and talks.
precondition: Staff and suppliers describe their work publicly.
detection: Reports from staff of unusual contact; spikes in profile views are weak signals.

assessment.question: Which roles with command or release authority can be identified and contacted from public sources?
assessment.evidence: A list of exposed privileged roles and the technologies their adverts reveal.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm exposed roles have stronger sign-in and are covered by targeted awareness.

name: Supply chain and component mapping
description: Work out which suppliers, components, frameworks and service providers the mission relies on, looking for the weakest.
precondition: Supplier relationships are visible through contracts, press, hardware teardown or software artefacts.
detection: Supplier-side reports of targeting; otherwise not detectable.

assessment.question: Which single supplier, if compromised, reaches the most missions or the most privileged function?
assessment.evidence: A dependency map ranking suppliers by reach into flight and operations.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm an alternative exists, or a compensating check, for the highest-ranked supplier.

name: Exposed infrastructure discovery
description: Scan and search for internet-reachable modems, antenna controllers, remote-access appliances, portals and service endpoints.
precondition: Mission or station equipment is reachable from the internet, deliberately or by mistake.
detection: Scan traffic at the perimeter; exposure-monitoring services reporting your own assets.

assessment.question: What mission-related management interfaces can be reached from the internet today?
assessment.evidence: An inventory of externally reachable services with owner and justification.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm each exposed service can be withdrawn quickly without stopping operations.

name: Clear-text traffic survey
description: Listen to unencrypted user or backhaul traffic on broad satellite beams to learn about the networks and people using them.
precondition: Traffic on the link is not encrypted and the beam covers the listener.
detection: Not detectable on the link; only an audit of what is sent in clear reveals the exposure.

assessment.question: What internal addressing, credentials or operational content crosses our space links unencrypted?
assessment.evidence: A classified sample of the mission's own link traffic showing what is readable.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm encryption can be enabled per service without breaking legacy users.

name: Operational rhythm analysis
description: Infer shift patterns, pass schedules, manoeuvre campaigns and critical periods such as early operations or eclipse seasons.
precondition: Regular operations leave observable patterns in emissions, schedules or announcements.
detection: Not directly detectable; note which critical periods are announced in advance.

assessment.question: When is our team thinnest and the spacecraft least forgiving, and could an outsider predict it?
assessment.evidence: A calendar of critical periods and how each could be predicted externally.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm staffing and authority to respond are no weaker in those periods.

name: Credential and code leak mining
description: Search public repositories, breach collections and criminal markets for mission credentials, tokens, keys and source code.
precondition: Staff or suppliers have leaked secrets or reused credentials exposed elsewhere.
detection: Secret scanning of repositories; monitoring of breach data for corporate identities.

assessment.question: Do any live credentials, tokens or keys for mission systems exist outside our control?
assessment.evidence: Results of a leak search across repositories and breach data, with validity of each finding.
assessment.recovery_test: Rotate one exposed secret end to end and measure the time and side effects.

name: Radio capability acquisition
description: Obtain the antennas, amplifiers and software-defined radios needed to receive from, transmit to or interfere with a space link.
precondition: The required band and power are within reach of commercial equipment.
detection: Spectrum monitoring sees test emissions; procurement is invisible to the operator.

assessment.question: What equipment budget buys a credible uplink or interference capability against each of our links?
assessment.evidence: A link-budget estimate of adversary capability per link, with assumptions.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; use the result to size margin and authentication requirements.

name: Ground-station service acquisition
description: Buy, borrow or fraudulently obtain time on commercial ground stations able to reach the target's bands and orbit.
precondition: Providers sell antenna time with limited checks on which spacecraft a customer may contact.
detection: Provider-side licensing checks; operator-side detection of unexpected uplink carriers.

assessment.question: Would our provider let another customer point at and transmit to our spacecraft?
assessment.evidence: Provider's written controls on licence verification and transmit authorisation.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm spacecraft authentication holds even if a compliant station transmits on our frequency.

name: Target replica construction
description: Build a working copy of the target from commercial components, open flight software and recovered documentation to rehearse against.
precondition: Components or software used by the mission are commercially or openly available.
detection: Unusual purchases reported by vendors; otherwise not detectable.

assessment.question: How much of our flight stack could a third party run on its own bench?
assessment.evidence: A list of flight components and software an outsider could acquire, with versions.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; assume rehearsal is possible and rely on keys, not novelty.

name: Flight software vulnerability research
description: Analyse flight software obtained from updates, development kits, partners or open source for flaws reachable by command or data.
precondition: The adversary has a copy of the flight software or the framework it is built on.
detection: Not detectable; rely on your own testing finding the same flaws first.

assessment.question: Has our command and data handling code been tested against malformed input from every external interface?
assessment.evidence: Fuzzing and review coverage reports for command, file-transfer and payload interfaces.
assessment.recovery_test: Patch one finding through the normal upload path on a flatsat and time the full cycle.

name: User terminal teardown and firmware extraction
description: Buy a terminal, open it and read out its firmware, keys and management protocol to study how the wider network trusts it.
precondition: Terminals are sold to the public or can be acquired second-hand.
detection: Tamper signals from terminals; anomalous devices on the network.

assessment.question: What does one purchased terminal reveal about every other terminal and about the gateway?
assessment.evidence: A teardown report listing extractable secrets and whether they are shared across the fleet.
assessment.recovery_test: Revoke one test terminal's identity and confirm the network refuses it.

name: Ground product vulnerability research
description: Find or buy flaws in mission-control software, station equipment, modems and remote-access appliances used by the sector.
precondition: Ground products are commercially available or exposed to the internet.
detection: Vendor advisories and sector reporting; exploitation attempts at the perimeter.

assessment.question: For each ground product, how quickly do we learn of a flaw and how long are we exposed?
assessment.evidence: Patch timelines for the last three relevant advisories.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm operations can continue with a vulnerable product isolated.

name: Cryptographic weakness identification
description: Look for absent, legacy, proprietary or misused cryptography: static keys, missing counters, unauthenticated modes or fallbacks.
precondition: The design predates modern link security or has an unprotected fallback mode.
detection: Not detectable; found by design review and lab testing.

assessment.question: Is there any mode, including safe mode and early operations, in which commands are accepted without authentication?
assessment.evidence: A matrix of spacecraft modes against authentication, encryption and anti-replay state.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm keys can be changed if an algorithm or key is found weak.

name: Access purchase from brokers
description: Buy working remote access, sessions or credentials for a space organisation or its supplier from criminal access brokers.
precondition: A device or account in the organisation is already compromised by commodity malware or phishing.
detection: Threat-intelligence monitoring of access sales; sign-ins from unfamiliar infrastructure.

assessment.question: If one employee's saved sessions were stolen today, what could the buyer reach?
assessment.evidence: Session and token inventory for a sample of privileged users, with lifetime and reach.
assessment.recovery_test: Invalidate all sessions for a test user and confirm access ends everywhere.

name: Tainted component or software staging
description: Prepare altered hardware, firmware or software to be introduced through a supplier, distributor or open-source project.
precondition: A supplier or project in the mission's chain accepts contributions or handles components without strong provenance checks.
detection: Provenance verification, incoming inspection and reproducible-build mismatches.

assessment.question: Which incoming items are trusted because of who delivered them rather than what was verified?
assessment.evidence: Provenance records for a sample of flight parts and software dependencies.
assessment.recovery_test: Replace a suspect component in the build and confirm the system can be re-verified.

name: Cover identity and infrastructure setup
description: Create front companies, customer accounts, academic personas or look-alike domains to approach staff or buy services.
precondition: The organisation or its providers accept new customers and partners with light verification.
detection: Know-your-customer checks; look-alike domain monitoring; staff reporting.

assessment.question: How would a fictitious customer or collaborator be vetted before receiving data, access or antenna time?
assessment.evidence: The onboarding record for a recent external party showing checks performed.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Legacy and unpatchable asset identification
description: Single out spacecraft and ground equipment that cannot be updated, lack link security or run end-of-life software.
precondition: Long-lived assets remain in service beyond the support life of their technology.
detection: Not detectable; known from your own asset register.

assessment.question: Which assets cannot be fixed if a flaw is found, and what protects them instead?
assessment.evidence: A register of unpatchable assets with compensating controls and retirement dates.
assessment.recovery_test: Exercise loss of the oldest asset and confirm the mission continues.

name: Insider recruitment or coercion
description: Persuade, pay or pressure someone with legitimate access to provide information, credentials or actions.
precondition: A person with access is identifiable and susceptible to approach.
detection: Behavioural indicators, access outside role or hours, staff reporting approaches.

assessment.question: Which single individual could cause the worst mission effect, and what would stop or reveal it?
assessment.evidence: A separation-of-duties review for command, key and release functions.
assessment.recovery_test: Remove one privileged person's access in an exercise and confirm nothing depends on them alone.

name: Targeted phishing of space-sector staff
description: Send tailored lures, often themed on conferences, jobs or partners, to obtain credentials or run code on staff devices.
precondition: Staff can be contacted and their devices or accounts have a route towards mission systems.
detection: Mail filtering, sign-in anomalies, endpoint alerts and staff reports.

assessment.question: If an operator's laptop is compromised by a lure, what stands between it and the command console?
assessment.evidence: Results of an authorised phishing exercise and the path traced from one compromised user.
assessment.recovery_test: Rebuild a compromised operator workstation and rotate its credentials within a target time.

name: Exploitation of internet-facing ground infrastructure
description: Exploit a flaw or misconfiguration in a remote-access appliance, portal or station device reachable from the internet.
precondition: A vulnerable or misconfigured device is exposed and leads towards management networks.
detection: Perimeter telemetry, appliance integrity checks and unexpected sessions from the device.

assessment.question: Which internet-facing device, if taken over, gives a route to station or fleet management?
assessment.evidence: Exposure scan plus a network path analysis from each exposed device.
assessment.recovery_test: Take one remote-access appliance out of service and confirm operations continue on an alternative.

name: Use of valid mission accounts
description: Sign in with stolen, guessed, sprayed or shared credentials to remote access, operations tools or cloud consoles.
precondition: Accounts lack strong multi-factor sign-in or sessions can be reused.
detection: Impossible travel, new devices, spray patterns and sign-ins outside shift patterns.

assessment.question: Can any mission role be exercised with a password alone, or with a session copied from another machine?
assessment.evidence: Sign-in policy export and a sample of mission-role authentications.
assessment.recovery_test: Disable and re-issue credentials for an entire shift team in an exercise.

name: Compromise of a cloud or station-service tenant
description: Take over the operator's account with a cloud or ground-station provider using stolen keys, tokens or console access.
precondition: Service credentials are long-lived, over-scoped or stored where they can be stolen.
detection: Provider audit logs showing new keys, unusual scheduling or access from new locations.

assessment.question: What could someone holding our provider API key schedule, download or change?
assessment.evidence: Scope and age of every provider credential, and an audit-log sample for one week.
assessment.recovery_test: Rotate provider credentials during an exercise without missing a pass.

name: Software supply chain compromise
description: Insert malicious code through a dependency, framework, vendor update or build service that the mission consumes.
precondition: The mission builds on third-party code or accepts vendor updates without independent verification.
detection: Dependency pinning alerts, build reproducibility checks and behaviour change after updates.

assessment.question: Could a change in one upstream dependency reach flight or operations without a human reviewing it?
assessment.evidence: Dependency inventory with pinning and review status for flight and ground builds.
assessment.recovery_test: Roll back a ground product update and rebuild flight software without a suspect dependency.

name: Hardware supply chain implant
description: Alter or substitute a component, board or programmable device before integration so it carries hidden function into orbit.
precondition: Parts pass through hands or facilities outside the operator's control without tamper evidence.
detection: Incoming inspection, electrical characterisation and custody records.

assessment.question: For which flight parts could a substitution go unnoticed between manufacture and integration?
assessment.evidence: Chain-of-custody records for a critical part and the inspection actually performed.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm a suspected unit could be isolated on orbit by switching to a redundant chain from a different lot.

name: Compromise of integration and test equipment
description: Use test benches, ground support equipment or loading tools that touch the spacecraft before launch as the way in.
precondition: Test equipment is networked, shared or maintained by third parties and is trusted by the spacecraft.
detection: Integrity checks of test tools; comparison of loaded images against signed releases.

assessment.question: Is what was loaded during integration provably the release that was approved?
assessment.evidence: Hash comparison between approved images and those read back from the unit after loading.
assessment.recovery_test: Re-load and attest flight software after integration using an independent tool.

name: Rogue ground station uplink
description: Transmit towards the spacecraft from equipment the operator does not control, placing frames directly at the command receiver.
precondition: The spacecraft is in view and the uplink parameters are known.
detection: On-board counters of rejected frames, receiver lock outside scheduled passes and spectrum monitoring.

assessment.question: What does the spacecraft do with a correctly formatted frame from an unknown transmitter?
assessment.evidence: Lab record of rejected-frame telemetry when an unkeyed transmitter sends valid-format commands.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm rejected-frame floods do not block legitimate commanding.

name: User terminal as entry point
description: Use a modified or compromised terminal to reach gateway, management or other customers' traffic from inside the network.
precondition: Terminals are trusted by the network beyond what a customer device should be.
detection: Terminals speaking management protocols or scanning; unexpected firmware versions.

assessment.question: From a terminal we do not control, what management functions and neighbours are reachable?
assessment.evidence: Reachability test results from a test terminal towards management and peer addresses.
assessment.recovery_test: Quarantine a misbehaving terminal from the network centre and confirm the action is effective.

name: Abuse of trusted vendor access
description: Enter through a supplier's remote-support channel, shared account or managed service that already has a path into operations.
precondition: A third party holds standing access to mission or station systems.
detection: Vendor sessions outside change windows or from new origins; actions beyond the support scope.

assessment.question: Which vendors can reach mission systems right now, and who would notice if they did?
assessment.evidence: A list of standing third-party access paths with last use and approval record.
assessment.recovery_test: Cut all vendor access in an exercise and confirm operations continue.

name: Hosted payload or third-party application entry
description: Arrive on board as, or by compromising, a hosted payload, rideshare interface or customer application running on the spacecraft.
precondition: The platform hosts equipment or code from parties other than the operator.
detection: Bus traffic from the hosted item outside its interface control; resource use beyond allocation.

assessment.question: What can a hosted item send to the platform beyond its agreed interface?
assessment.evidence: Bus capture from a flatsat showing what the platform accepts from the hosted interface.
assessment.recovery_test: Power off or isolate the hosted item and confirm the platform is unaffected.

name: Physical intrusion at a ground site
description: Enter a remote or lightly staffed station to connect to equipment, networks or console ports.
precondition: Sites are remote, shared or unattended and equipment trusts local connections.
detection: Access control and video records; new devices on station networks.

assessment.question: What can someone standing in our most remote station do with a laptop and a cable?
assessment.evidence: A physical assessment report for one remote site including network port behaviour.
assessment.recovery_test: Remove the site from the network remotely and operate from another.

name: Removable media or engineering device into the mission enclave
description: Carry malicious code across an air gap or boundary on media, laptops or instruments used for maintenance and data transfer.
precondition: The enclave depends on manual transfers or visiting equipment.
detection: Media scanning stations, device control logs and new executables in the enclave.

assessment.question: How does software and data enter the mission enclave, and which path has the least inspection?
assessment.evidence: A record of every transfer into the enclave over one month with its inspection result.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Compromise of customer and tasking interfaces
description: Break into the portals and interfaces through which customers request tasking or collect products, as a route inward.
precondition: Customer-facing systems share data or networks with planning and operations.
detection: Abnormal request patterns, privilege changes and traffic from portal to internal systems.

assessment.question: Can a request submitted through the customer interface influence planning without validation?
assessment.evidence: A data-flow diagram from portal to planning with validation points marked and tested.
assessment.recovery_test: Take the customer interface offline and confirm operations and delivery by another route.

name: Crosslink or proximity radio access
description: Reach a spacecraft through its inter-satellite or proximity link from another spacecraft the adversary controls or has compromised.
precondition: The spacecraft accepts traffic on crosslinks and an adversary node can join or imitate the mesh.
detection: Unexpected link acquisitions; crosslink traffic from unknown identities.

assessment.question: Does a neighbour on the crosslink have any authority that the ground does not need a key to exercise?
assessment.evidence: A protocol review and simulator test of crosslink authentication and authorisation.
assessment.recovery_test: Disable crosslinks on one spacecraft and confirm it can still be operated directly.

name: Command replay
description: Record legitimate command transmissions and send them again later so the spacecraft repeats an action.
precondition: Commands are not bound to a counter or time window that the spacecraft enforces.
detection: Commands executed without a matching ground record; counter anomalies.

assessment.question: Will the spacecraft act twice on the same captured command frame?
assessment.evidence: Lab test record of a replayed frame and the resulting telemetry.
assessment.recovery_test: Confirm counters resynchronise safely after a reboot without opening a replay window.

name: Unauthenticated command injection
description: Send new, well-formed commands to a spacecraft that does not verify who sent them.
precondition: No command authentication, or a mode in which it is switched off.
detection: Command counters advancing without ground activity; state changes with no procedure.

assessment.question: In every mode, does the spacecraft refuse a valid-format command that lacks proof of origin?
assessment.evidence: Mode-by-mode lab results for unauthenticated commands.
assessment.recovery_test: Regain exclusive control on a flatsat after a simulated third-party command.

name: Command injection from a compromised mission control system
description: Issue commands through the operator's own control system so they arrive correctly authenticated.
precondition: The adversary holds a position in mission operations with rights to send or queue commands.
detection: Commands with no approved procedure, unusual operator or unusual time; mismatch with the pass plan.

assessment.question: If the control system is hostile, which commands still need something the attacker does not have?
assessment.evidence: A list of hazardous commands and the independent approval each requires, tested in the twin.
assessment.recovery_test: Command the twin from the alternate site while the primary control system is treated as compromised.

name: Abuse of stored and scheduled commanding
description: Load time-tagged commands, on-board procedures or macros that execute later, out of contact and out of sight.
precondition: The spacecraft supports stored sequences and the adversary can load or edit them.
detection: Differences between the on-board schedule and the approved plan; unexpected sequence activations.

assessment.question: Is the on-board schedule read back and compared with the approved plan at every contact?
assessment.evidence: A schedule read-back comparison procedure and its last results.
assessment.recovery_test: Clear and reload the on-board schedule from a trusted source on the twin.

name: Malicious flight software upload
description: Use the legitimate patch or image upload service to place altered software on the spacecraft.
precondition: Uploads are not verified on board against a signature the adversary cannot produce.
detection: Image hashes that differ from the approved release; unscheduled upload activity.

assessment.question: Will the spacecraft activate an image that was not signed by the release authority?
assessment.evidence: Flatsat record of refused unsigned and wrongly signed images.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore the protected image on the flatsat and attest it independently.

name: Exploitation of on-board input handling
description: Send malformed commands, files or data that trigger a flaw in on-board parsing and yield unintended execution.
precondition: A reachable flaw exists in code that handles external input.
detection: Unexpected resets, memory faults, watchdog events and rejected-frame patterns.

assessment.question: Which on-board parsers face external input and how were they tested?
assessment.evidence: Fuzzing coverage and crash triage for each externally reachable parser.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover the flatsat from a forced processor fault and verify image integrity.

name: Abuse of maintenance, debug or bootloader modes
description: Enter low-level service modes that offer memory access or image loading with weaker protection than normal operations.
precondition: Service modes remain reachable after launch or in safe mode.
detection: Mode transitions without a procedure; memory load or dump commands.

assessment.question: What can be done in bootloader or maintenance mode, and what proves the requester is entitled?
assessment.evidence: A list of service-mode functions with the authentication each demands, tested on the flatsat.
assessment.recovery_test: Exit service mode to a verified image using only the documented recovery procedure.

name: Privilege escalation in the ground environment
description: Move from an ordinary foothold to directory, virtualisation or operations administrator rights.
precondition: Enterprise and mission administration share identities, hosts or management tools.
detection: Directory change alerts, credential-theft tooling and new privileged group members.

assessment.question: Does compromise of the corporate directory grant any right inside the mission enclave?
assessment.evidence: An identity trust map between enterprise and mission, with an authorised test of one path.
assessment.recovery_test: Rebuild mission identity services from a trusted backup in the range.

name: Command key or crypto-state compromise
description: Obtain command keys, or the ability to use them, from ground key stores, operations tools or poorly protected backups.
precondition: Keys are reachable in software, exported for convenience or usable by a single administrator.
detection: Key-use records outside passes; key export or backup events; administrator actions on key stores.

assessment.question: Can any one person or one compromised host use or copy the command key?
assessment.evidence: Key-ceremony records and a test showing key use requires hardware and dual control.
assessment.recovery_test: Rehearse an on-orbit rekey on the flatsat from a declared key compromise.

name: Payload tasking hijack
description: Direct the payload without authority: retask a sensor, reconfigure a transponder or redirect capacity.
precondition: Payload control is reachable separately from, or with less protection than, platform commanding.
detection: Tasking that matches no customer order; payload configuration drift.

assessment.question: Is payload commanding protected to the same standard as platform commanding?
assessment.evidence: A comparison of authentication and approval for platform and payload command paths.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore payload configuration from a trusted baseline and reconcile outstanding orders.

name: Management-plane takeover of a terminal fleet
description: Gain control of the systems that configure and update user terminals, and so the ability to act on every terminal at once.
precondition: The management network is reachable from a compromised position and can issue fleet-wide actions.
detection: Bulk management commands, unusual update jobs and mass terminal state changes.

assessment.question: What is the largest number of terminals one management action can change, and what slows it down?
assessment.evidence: Evidence of rate limits and approvals for fleet-wide actions, tested on lab terminals.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore a batch of test terminals to service after a bad configuration push, without a site visit.

name: On-board privilege escalation
description: Move from a confined position on board, such as a payload or application, to control of platform functions.
precondition: Partitioning between on-board functions is weak or the data bus trusts every node.
detection: Bus messages from unexpected sources; tasks or resource use outside allocation.

assessment.question: Can a compromised payload issue platform commands over the on-board bus?
assessment.evidence: Flatsat bus-injection test results from the payload interface.
assessment.recovery_test: Isolate the payload and return the platform to a verified configuration.

name: Takeover of antenna control and station automation
description: Control the systems that point antennas, configure modems and run pass schedules, to deny, redirect or enable contacts.
precondition: Station automation is reachable on shared networks or through provider interfaces.
detection: Pointing, power or schedule changes that match no plan; missed passes.

assessment.question: Who can change what the antenna points at and transmits, and how is each change authorised?
assessment.evidence: Access-control review of station automation and a tested unauthorised schedule change in the range.
assessment.recovery_test: Run a pass manually with automation disabled.

name: Operator deception into harmful commanding
description: Lead operators to send damaging commands themselves by altering procedures, displays or planning inputs, or by impersonation.
precondition: Operators rely on documents, displays or requests whose integrity is not independently checked.
detection: Procedure changes outside configuration control; discrepancies between displays and raw telemetry.

assessment.question: Would an operator following a tampered procedure be stopped by anything before a hazardous command?
assessment.evidence: Configuration-control records for procedures and a twin exercise using an altered procedure.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore procedures and display definitions from a signed baseline.

name: Persistent flight software modification
description: Alter stored flight software or tables so the change survives resets and remains across operations.
precondition: Stored images or tables can be written without verification at next boot.
detection: Periodic memory checksums and attestation against the released image.

assessment.question: How often, and by what independent means, is on-board software compared with the release?
assessment.evidence: Latest on-board checksum results reconciled with release hashes.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore and attest a modified image on the flatsat.

name: Bootloader or recovery image tampering
description: Modify the first-stage loader or the fallback image so that even recovery starts from compromised code.
precondition: The root of trust is writable in flight or was compromised before launch.
detection: Attestation rooted in immutable hardware; pre-launch image verification.

assessment.question: Is there any software on board that cannot be altered by any command, and does recovery start from it?
assessment.evidence: Design evidence of an immutable root and a test attempting to rewrite it.
assessment.recovery_test: Demonstrate recovery from the immutable root with every writable image assumed hostile.

name: Persistence in ground mission systems
description: Install services, tasks, accounts or implants on operations hosts so access outlasts reboots and password changes.
precondition: The adversary holds administrative rights on ground hosts.
detection: Endpoint detection, baseline drift, new services and scheduled tasks.

assessment.question: How would we know a mission-control server carries software that is not in its baseline?
assessment.evidence: Baseline comparison of one operations host against its approved build.
assessment.recovery_test: Rebuild the host from trusted media and return it to operations.

name: Telemetry masking
description: Alter telemetry on board or on the ground so operators see nominal values while the real state differs.
precondition: The adversary controls a point in the telemetry chain and telemetry is not independently verifiable.
detection: Cross-checks between independent sensors, physics models, external tracking and raw link metrics.

assessment.question: Which telemetry values could be false without any independent measurement contradicting them?
assessment.evidence: A table of critical parameters with their independent cross-check, exercised in the twin.
assessment.recovery_test: Establish true state using only independent sources in an exercise.

name: Ground command log and audit tampering
description: Delete or edit command histories, operator logs and security records to hide what was sent and by whom.
precondition: Logs are stored where operations administrators can change them.
detection: Gaps or hash-chain breaks in logs; disagreement between ground history and on-board counters.

assessment.question: Can an operations administrator alter the command history without leaving evidence elsewhere?
assessment.evidence: Evidence that logs are forwarded to a store operations staff cannot modify.
assessment.recovery_test: Reconstruct one pass's commanding from independent sources only.

name: On-board event and counter suppression
description: Disable event reporting, clear error logs or reset counters on board so intrusion leaves no trace in telemetry.
precondition: Event reporting and counters can be reconfigured by command.
detection: Event filters or counters changed outside procedure; counters that fail to advance.

assessment.question: Which commands can silence on-board reporting, and are they treated as hazardous?
assessment.evidence: List of reporting-control commands and their classification.
assessment.recovery_test: Reset reporting configuration to baseline on the flatsat and verify by test event.

name: Fault protection manipulation
description: Disable or retune on-board fault detection and response so abnormal conditions are tolerated or responses are harmful.
precondition: Fault-protection thresholds and enables are changeable by command or table load.
detection: Table read-back differences; fault monitors disabled without an approved waiver.

assessment.question: Could fault protection be switched off, or its limits widened, without a second approval?
assessment.evidence: Fault-protection table comparison against baseline and the approval record for each change.
assessment.recovery_test: Reload baseline fault-protection tables on the flatsat and inject a test fault.

name: Living off mission tooling
description: Use the operator's own administration tools, scripts and procedures so activity looks like routine work.
precondition: The adversary has valid access and the environment has rich built-in tooling.
detection: Behavioural baselines per role and shift; use of tools by accounts that never use them.

assessment.question: Would we notice legitimate tools being used by the wrong person or at the wrong time?
assessment.evidence: An analytic that flags out-of-role tool use, tested with a benign simulation.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Rogue keys, accounts or stations
description: Add an operator account, authorise an extra station or load an additional key so access continues after a clean-up.
precondition: Key slots, station lists or account stores can be extended without independent review.
detection: Inventory checks of on-board key slots, station authorisations and privileged accounts.

assessment.question: Do we know exactly which keys, stations and accounts are authorised, and when that last changed?
assessment.evidence: A reconciled inventory of keys, authorised stations and privileged accounts.
assessment.recovery_test: Revoke an unrecognised key on the flatsat and confirm it no longer authenticates.

name: Persistence in terminal firmware
description: Modify terminal firmware or bootloaders so compromise survives factory reset and operator updates.
precondition: Terminal firmware is not verified at boot or signing keys are exposed.
detection: Firmware version and hash reporting from the fleet; terminals refusing updates.

assessment.question: Can we prove what firmware each terminal is running without trusting the terminal?
assessment.evidence: Remote attestation or hash-reporting evidence for a sample of terminals.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover a lab terminal with modified firmware to a verified state remotely.

name: Dormant, condition-triggered logic
description: Place code that waits for a date, orbital position, command pattern or mission phase before acting.
precondition: Code can be introduced before launch or by update and is not fully reviewed or exercised.
detection: Code review, coverage analysis and comparison of flown images with reproducible builds.

assessment.question: How much flown code has never been executed in test, and who reviewed it?
assessment.evidence: Coverage figures for flight software and a list of unexercised regions.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; address through build integrity and trusted recovery.

name: Hiding in payloads and unmonitored subsystems
description: Reside in programmable logic, radio payloads or processors that the platform does not inspect and operators rarely read back.
precondition: Reconfigurable devices on board lack integrity monitoring.
detection: Configuration read-back and comparison; unexpected resource use or emissions.

assessment.question: Which programmable devices on board have never had their configuration read back in orbit?
assessment.evidence: Inventory of reconfigurable devices with read-back capability and last verification date.
assessment.recovery_test: Reload a payload configuration from the trusted baseline and verify it.

name: Persistence in the build and update channel
description: Stay inside source control, build servers or update distribution so every new release is compromised again.
precondition: Build infrastructure is reachable from compromised networks and signs what it builds.
detection: Build provenance, reproducibility checks and monitoring of build-system changes.

assessment.question: If the build server were compromised, would the signature on the next release still be valid?
assessment.evidence: Evidence that signing is separated from building and that releases are reproducible.
assessment.recovery_test: Rebuild the pipeline from scratch in an exercise and re-issue a release.

name: Operating in visibility gaps
description: Act while the spacecraft is out of contact, during handovers or when monitoring is known to be reduced.
precondition: There are predictable periods with no ground visibility or reduced staffing.
detection: On-board logging of all command sources; store-and-forward event records reviewed at next contact.

assessment.question: Is anything the spacecraft does while out of contact recorded on board and reviewed afterwards?
assessment.evidence: A sample of out-of-contact event logs and the review record.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Enterprise to mission operations pivot
description: Move from corporate IT into mission operations through shared services, jump hosts, file transfers or administrator habits.
precondition: There is at least one network, identity or data path between enterprise and mission environments.
detection: Boundary traffic outside the approved list; enterprise identities appearing in mission logs.

assessment.question: List every path from enterprise to mission. Which one would an intruder use?
assessment.evidence: Boundary rule review and an authorised attempt to cross from enterprise to mission.
assessment.recovery_test: Sever all enterprise connections and operate the mission in isolation for a set period.

name: Ground to space through the legitimate uplink
description: Use the operator's command chain as the bridge to the spacecraft once ground operations are compromised.
precondition: Ground compromise reaches a system able to release commands or uploads.
detection: Independent reconciliation of released commands against approvals.

assessment.question: After ground compromise, what further barrier exists before the spacecraft is affected?
assessment.evidence: Description and test of controls that sit between a compromised console and the transmitter.
assessment.recovery_test: Hold all commanding, then resume from the alternate site with verified procedures.

name: Space to ground through hostile downlinked data
description: Send crafted telemetry or payload data that exploits the ground software which parses it, turning the downlink into an attack path.
precondition: Ground software trusts downlinked data and the adversary controls a spacecraft, a signal or the data.
detection: Parser crashes, malformed-frame counts and unexpected processes on ingest hosts.

assessment.question: Is data from space treated as untrusted input by every ground component that parses it?
assessment.evidence: Fuzzing results for telemetry and payload ingest, and the isolation of ingest hosts.
assessment.recovery_test: Rebuild an ingest host and replay stored data through a hardened parser.

name: Payload and platform crossover on the data bus
description: Cross between payload and platform domains using the shared on-board bus, shared memory or shared processors.
precondition: Domains share a bus or computing resource without enforced separation.
detection: Bus monitors reporting unexpected message sources or types.

assessment.question: What enforces the boundary between payload and platform, and has it been tested by injection?
assessment.evidence: Bus-level test results for cross-domain message injection on the flatsat.
assessment.recovery_test: Isolate one domain and operate the other.

name: Spacecraft to spacecraft across the constellation
description: Spread from one spacecraft to others over crosslinks, shared routing or peer software distribution.
precondition: Spacecraft trust traffic or software from their neighbours.
detection: Anomalies appearing in sequence along the mesh; unexpected peer-to-peer control traffic.

assessment.question: If one spacecraft is hostile, what can it make its neighbours do?
assessment.evidence: Simulator results for a misbehaving node, including routing and control-plane effects.
assessment.recovery_test: Eject a node from the mesh and confirm the remainder keeps serving.

name: Station to station across shared networks
description: Move between ground stations, or from one operator's equipment to another's, over provider or wide-area networks.
precondition: Stations share management networks, credentials or a provider backbone.
detection: East-west traffic between sites outside the approved pattern.

assessment.question: Can a compromised station reach the others, or other tenants' equipment at the same site?
assessment.evidence: Inter-site firewall review and an authorised lateral-movement test.
assessment.recovery_test: Remove one station from the network and continue operations.

name: Tenant to tenant in shared ground services
description: Cross from one customer's environment to another's inside a shared cloud or ground-station service.
precondition: The provider's isolation between customers has a flaw or a shared component.
detection: Provider-reported isolation events; your resources appearing in another context.

assessment.question: What evidence does the provider give that another customer cannot see or act on our contacts and data?
assessment.evidence: Provider isolation attestations and results of any permitted customer-side test.
assessment.recovery_test: Fail over to a second provider or own station for a set of passes.

name: User terminal to gateway and core
description: Travel from the customer edge inward to gateway, management and core network systems.
precondition: The return path from terminals is not filtered as untrusted customer traffic.
detection: Terminal-originated traffic to management addresses; protocol misuse at the gateway.

assessment.question: Is traffic arriving from terminals filtered as hostile before it reaches management systems?
assessment.evidence: Gateway filtering rules and a test from a lab terminal.
assessment.recovery_test: Block a terminal population at the gateway without affecting others.

name: Vendor to customers through trusted distribution
description: Use one supplier's update, support or management channel to reach many operators at once.
precondition: Many operators accept the same vendor's updates or remote management.
detection: Staged roll-out telemetry; behaviour change after vendor updates; sector alerts.

assessment.question: Would a malicious vendor update reach production before anyone outside the vendor had examined it?
assessment.evidence: The update acceptance procedure and evidence of staged deployment.
assessment.recovery_test: Roll back a vendor update across a test population.

name: Fleet-wide propagation through constellation operations
description: Use automation that manages many spacecraft to push the same harmful change to the whole constellation.
precondition: Operations tooling can apply a change to all spacecraft without staging.
detection: Change-rate monitoring; canary spacecraft diverging after an update.

assessment.question: What is the minimum time and number of approvals to change software on every spacecraft?
assessment.evidence: Roll-out policy showing staging, canaries and halt criteria, exercised in the twin.
assessment.recovery_test: Halt a roll-out part-way and return affected spacecraft to the previous image.

name: Development and test to operations bridge
description: Cross from simulators, test benches or development networks into operations through shared tools, data or connections.
precondition: Test environments connect to operations for data, licences or convenience.
detection: Traffic between test and operations networks; test credentials seen in operations.

assessment.question: Is there any standing connection or shared credential between test and operations?
assessment.evidence: Network and identity review between test and operations environments.
assessment.recovery_test: Disconnect test from operations and confirm both still function.

name: Cross-mission pivot through shared services
description: Move from one mission to another through shared key management, flight dynamics, networks or operations teams.
precondition: Several missions depend on a common service that trusts all of them.
detection: Service access by one mission's identities to another mission's resources.

assessment.question: Which shared services, if compromised through one mission, expose the others?
assessment.evidence: A shared-service inventory with per-mission isolation evidence.
assessment.recovery_test: Operate one mission with a shared service unavailable.

name: Hosted payload to host operator ground
description: Use the ground interfaces that serve a hosted payload's owner as a route into the host operator's systems, or the reverse.
precondition: Hosted-payload operations centres connect into the host's ground segment.
detection: Traffic from the hosted-payload interface beyond its agreed services.

assessment.question: What can the hosted-payload owner's network reach inside ours?
assessment.evidence: Interface control review and firewall evidence for the hosted-payload connection.
assessment.recovery_test: Suspend the hosted-payload interface and confirm host operations are unaffected.

name: Downlink eavesdropping
description: Receive and read mission data, user traffic or telemetry that is sent without effective encryption.
precondition: The listener is in the footprint and the traffic is readable.
detection: Not detectable on the link; audit what is sent in clear.

assessment.question: Which data on our links could a third party read today?
assessment.evidence: Per-link statement of encryption state, verified by lab capture.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Mission data theft from ground processing
description: Copy payload data, products or customer information from processing systems, archives and distribution platforms.
precondition: The adversary has access to systems where mission data is stored or processed.
detection: Large or unusual reads from archives; new access keys; egress volume anomalies.

assessment.question: Would bulk copying of our archive be noticed, and how quickly?
assessment.evidence: A data-egress detection test using a benign bulk download.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; confirm notification obligations and customer communication plan.

name: Exfiltration or control over satellite links
description: Use satellite connectivity, including other parties' unencrypted downlinks, to carry stolen data or hide control traffic.
precondition: Broad beams allow receive-only collection of traffic addressed to someone else.
detection: Unexpected destinations within satellite address ranges; unsolicited traffic towards idle users.

assessment.question: Could our link capacity or address space be carrying someone else's hidden traffic?
assessment.evidence: Traffic analysis for flows towards addresses with no active customer.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable.

name: Payload data tampering
description: Alter imagery, measurements or other products in processing or on board so that users receive false information.
precondition: Products are not sealed at source and can be changed before delivery.
detection: Signature or hash failures; statistical checks against independent sources.

assessment.question: Could a product be changed between sensor and customer without any check failing?
assessment.evidence: End-to-end integrity test with a deliberately altered product in staging.
assessment.recovery_test: Reprocess a product from raw data held in a protected archive.

name: Orbit and conjunction data manipulation
description: Change ephemerides, tracking inputs or conjunction warnings so that operators plan manoeuvres on false data or miss real ones.
precondition: Flight dynamics relies on inputs or files whose integrity is not verified.
detection: Comparison with independent tracking; unexplained residuals in orbit determination.

assessment.question: Do we verify orbit and conjunction data against a second source before manoeuvring?
assessment.evidence: Procedure and records showing independent verification before the last manoeuvre.
assessment.recovery_test: Recompute an orbit solution from raw tracking on a clean system.

name: On-board parameter and table tampering
description: Change control gains, limits, calibration or configuration tables to degrade performance subtly over time.
precondition: Tables can be loaded by command and are not regularly compared with baseline.
detection: Table checksums and read-back; performance trending.

assessment.question: How long could a small unauthorised change to a control table go unnoticed?
assessment.evidence: Table read-back schedule and last comparison results.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore baseline tables on the flatsat and confirm performance recovers.

name: Time and clock manipulation
description: Shift on-board or ground time so schedules, counters, key validity or data time-tags behave incorrectly.
precondition: Time is set by command or taken from a single external source.
detection: Divergence between independent clocks; time-tagged commands executing early or late.

assessment.question: What breaks if spacecraft or ground time is wrong by a minute, an hour or a year?
assessment.evidence: Twin results for stepped time offsets, including anti-replay and schedule behaviour.
assessment.recovery_test: Resynchronise time from a trusted source and confirm counters and schedules recover.

name: Sensor deception on board
description: Present false stimuli to on-board sensors such as navigation receivers so the spacecraft's own estimate of its state is wrong.
precondition: The spacecraft relies on an external signal or scene that can be imitated.
detection: Disagreement between redundant or dissimilar sensors; innovation checks in estimators.

assessment.question: Which on-board sensors can be influenced from outside, and what cross-checks them?
assessment.evidence: Simulation of a false navigation input and the estimator's response.
assessment.recovery_test: Reject the affected sensor and continue on dissimilar sensing.

name: Navigation signal spoofing against users
description: Broadcast counterfeit navigation signals so receivers report a false position or time.
precondition: Receivers accept unauthenticated signals and the adversary can overpower the genuine ones locally.
detection: Position or time jumps, signal-power anomalies and disagreement with inertial or other sources.

assessment.question: Which of our services or users would accept a false position or time, and what would it cause?
assessment.evidence: Cabled spoofing test results for representative receivers.
assessment.recovery_test: Operate the service on an alternative position or time source for a set period.

name: Key and crypto-configuration theft
description: Copy keys, key-loading files or crypto configuration from ground stores, backups, test equipment or suppliers.
precondition: Key material exists outside hardware protection at some point in its life.
detection: Access records for key stores and backups; discovery of key material in unexpected places.

assessment.question: Trace one key from generation to spacecraft. Where is it ever in a form that can be copied?
assessment.evidence: A key life-cycle walk-through with evidence at each step.
assessment.recovery_test: Rehearse rekey of ground and space after a declared theft.

name: Unauthorised use of transponder capacity
description: Transmit through a bent-pipe transponder without permission, consuming power and bandwidth for the adversary's own traffic.
precondition: The transponder relays whatever it receives in band.
detection: Carrier monitoring showing unassigned carriers; geolocation of the uplink source.

assessment.question: How quickly would we detect and locate a carrier we did not assign?
assessment.evidence: Carrier-monitoring detection time for a test carrier.
assessment.recovery_test: Reassign affected customers and reconfigure the transponder plan.

name: Mission planning and tasking data manipulation
description: Alter schedules, pass plans or tasking queues so the mission does the wrong thing at the wrong time without any hostile command.
precondition: Planning products move between systems without integrity protection or review.
detection: Plan-versus-execution reconciliation; unexplained plan changes.

assessment.question: Could someone change tomorrow's plan without the planner or operator noticing?
assessment.evidence: Integrity and approval evidence for planning products, tested with an altered plan in staging.
assessment.recovery_test: Regenerate plans from validated inputs on a clean system.

name: Traffic interception at gateways and operator networks
description: Collect or alter customer traffic where it leaves the satellite network, from a position inside operator or gateway systems.
precondition: The adversary has access to gateway, core or lawful-intercept-like functions.
detection: Configuration changes on core devices; unexpected mirroring or tunnels.

assessment.question: Who can configure traffic mirroring or routing at our gateways, and is every change reviewed?
assessment.evidence: Configuration audit of gateway devices against baseline.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore gateway configuration from baseline and rotate device credentials.

name: Design and intellectual property exfiltration
description: Steal designs, source code, interface documents and test data that make later attacks on the mission easier.
precondition: Engineering data sits on enterprise or supplier systems reachable from a foothold.
detection: Data-loss monitoring; unusual repository cloning; archive creation on engineering hosts.

assessment.question: If our design repository were copied, which protections would lose their value?
assessment.evidence: A list of controls that depend on design secrecy, and repository access analytics.
assessment.recovery_test: Not applicable; reassess the threat model assuming the adversary holds the design.

name: Uplink jamming
description: Transmit interference at the spacecraft's receiver so commands or user uplinks cannot be received.
precondition: The adversary is in the receive beam with sufficient power.
detection: Receiver noise-floor and lock telemetry; failed command verification; spectrum monitoring.

assessment.question: How long can the spacecraft operate safely without commands, and can we command from elsewhere?
assessment.evidence: Autonomy duration analysis and a cabled interference test.
assessment.recovery_test: Command through a different station, band or beam in an exercise.

name: Downlink jamming
description: Interfere with reception at ground stations or user terminals so telemetry or service is lost locally.
precondition: The adversary is near the receiver.
detection: Signal-to-noise drops across terminals in an area; station receiver alarms.

assessment.question: Which stations and user areas can be denied by a local emitter, and what is the fallback?
assessment.evidence: Interference margin per receive site and a tested fallback.
assessment.recovery_test: Shift reception to another site or beam.

name: Navigation signal jamming
description: Overpower navigation signals so receivers lose position and time.
precondition: Navigation signals are weak at the receiver and cheap emitters exist.
detection: Loss of lock across receivers; carrier-to-noise drops; interference reports.

assessment.question: Which of our systems fail, and how, when satellite navigation is unavailable for a day?
assessment.evidence: Hold-over test results for timing and navigation-dependent systems.
assessment.recovery_test: Run on alternative timing and navigation for the tested period.

name: Terminal fleet wipe or disablement
description: Send destructive commands or software to user terminals at scale so they stop working and cannot be recovered remotely.
precondition: The adversary controls a channel that can reach many terminals with privileged actions.
detection: Mass terminal drop-off; destructive commands on the management plane.

assessment.question: If a large share of terminals were disabled tonight, how would service be restored and how fast?
assessment.evidence: A recovery plan with stock, logistics and re-provisioning time, tested on lab terminals.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover wiped lab terminals and measure time per unit and what needs a site visit.

name: Destruction or encryption of ground systems
description: Wipe or encrypt mission-control, station or processing systems so the operator cannot fly or deliver.
precondition: The adversary holds broad administrative access in the ground environment.
detection: Mass file changes, backup deletion and security tooling being disabled.

assessment.question: With every ground server in the primary site unusable, how long until we can command again?
assessment.evidence: Timed rebuild of mission control from offline backups.
assessment.recovery_test: Command a simulator from rebuilt systems or the alternate site.

name: Spacecraft denial of service
description: Drive the spacecraft into repeated resets, safe mode or receiver saturation so it cannot perform its mission.
precondition: The spacecraft reacts to hostile input or commands with protective shutdown.
detection: Reset counters, safe-mode entries and rejected-frame rates.

assessment.question: Can an outsider keep the spacecraft in safe mode indefinitely?
assessment.evidence: Flatsat test of behaviour under sustained invalid commanding.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover from safe mode under continued interference in the twin.

name: Consumable and resource exhaustion
description: Spend propellant, battery cycles, storage or thermal margin through commanded activity that shortens or ends the mission.
precondition: Resource-consuming commands are not limited or independently approved.
detection: Resource trend alarms; activity with no corresponding plan.

assessment.question: What is the fastest way to waste a year of mission life by command, and what would stop it?
assessment.evidence: Analysis of hazardous resource commands and their on-board limits.
assessment.recovery_test: Not recoverable once spent; verify limits and approvals prevent it in the twin.

name: Attitude or orbit control hijack
description: Command thrusters or attitude actuators to tumble the spacecraft, change its orbit or point it harmfully.
precondition: The adversary can issue control commands that the spacecraft accepts.
detection: Attitude and orbit deviations; actuator activity without a plan; independent tracking.

assessment.question: Which protections remain between a valid manoeuvre command and thruster firing?
assessment.evidence: List of arming steps and on-board limits for propulsion, tested in the twin.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover attitude from a tumbling state in the twin using safe-mode procedures.

name: Payload damage or misuse
description: Operate the payload outside safe limits or against its purpose, for example exposing a sensor or overdriving an amplifier.
precondition: Payload safety relies on correct commanding rather than on-board interlocks.
detection: Payload health limits; operations outside the plan.

assessment.question: Which payload-damaging actions are prevented on board rather than by procedure?
assessment.evidence: Interlock inventory for payload hazards.
assessment.recovery_test: Not recoverable if hardware is damaged; verify interlocks in the twin.

name: Permanent spacecraft disablement
description: Leave the spacecraft unusable by corrupting software beyond recovery or locking the operator out.
precondition: The adversary can write boot-critical software or change command keys.
detection: Loss of contact following image or key operations; attestation failures.

assessment.question: Is there any sequence of commands after which we could never regain the spacecraft?
assessment.evidence: Analysis of unrecoverable states and the protections around each.
assessment.recovery_test: Demonstrate recovery from the worst reachable state on the flatsat.

name: Broadcast or service hijack
description: Replace or override legitimate content or service on a transponder or distribution chain with the adversary's own.
precondition: The uplink can be overpowered or the distribution chain upstream is compromised.
detection: Content monitoring; unexpected uplink carriers; customer reports.

assessment.question: How fast can we detect and remove an intruding signal on a broadcast carrier?
assessment.evidence: Detection and response timing from a monitored test.
assessment.recovery_test: Move the service to another transponder or uplink site.

name: Deception of downstream users
description: Cause users to act on false products, positions or times, so the harm occurs in the dependent system rather than the space system.
precondition: Users trust the service output without independent checks.
detection: User-side plausibility checks; reports of inconsistent data.

assessment.question: Which customers would make a safety or financial decision on our data without checking it?
assessment.evidence: A register of safety-relevant users and the integrity signal they receive.
assessment.recovery_test: Issue a product recall or integrity warning to users in an exercise and time it.

name: Collision risk and debris generation
description: Use control of a spacecraft or of orbit data to raise collision risk for it and for others.
precondition: The adversary controls manoeuvring or the data used to plan it.
detection: Independent tracking and conjunction services; coordination with other operators.

assessment.question: Who would we tell, and how fast, if we lost control of a manoeuvrable spacecraft?
assessment.evidence: Notification procedure and contact list tested in an exercise.
assessment.recovery_test: Coordinate a simulated loss-of-control event with tracking and neighbouring operators.

name: Extortion over mission control or data
description: Demand payment or concessions by threatening to publish stolen data, withhold systems or misuse spacecraft control.
precondition: The adversary holds stolen data or disruptive access.
detection: Extortion contact; data appearing on leak sites; encryption activity.

assessment.question: Who decides how we respond to an extortion demand, and on what information?
assessment.evidence: A decision record from an extortion tabletop, including legal and regulator steps.
assessment.recovery_test: Operate and deliver while the affected systems are held out of service.

name: Denial of service against ground and customer services
description: Flood or exhaust internet-facing portals, sign-in services, gateways or provider interfaces so customers and operators cannot use them.
precondition: Services needed by users or operators are reachable from the internet with limited capacity protection.
detection: Traffic volume and error-rate alarms; upstream provider alerts; claims on social channels.

assessment.question: Which internet-facing service, if unavailable for a day, stops customers or operators working?
assessment.evidence: A dependency list of internet-facing services with capacity protection and tested fallback.
assessment.recovery_test: Operate with the affected service withdrawn and customers redirected to a fallback.

name: Safe-mode exploitation
description: Use the recovery state itself: safe mode that relaxes authentication, widens antenna coverage or accepts low-level commands.
precondition: Safe mode trades security for recoverability.
detection: Commanding during safe mode from unexpected sources; safe-mode entries with no natural cause.

assessment.question: Is the spacecraft easier to command for an outsider in safe mode than in normal mode?
assessment.evidence: Flatsat comparison of protections in normal and safe mode.
assessment.recovery_test: Recover from safe mode with authentication enforced throughout.

name: Recovery image and baseline corruption
description: Tamper with the images, baselines and procedures used for recovery so that restoring brings the compromise back.
precondition: Recovery material is stored where the adversary has been.
detection: Hash verification of recovery material against an offline record.

assessment.question: Where is our last known-good image, and how do we know it is good?
assessment.evidence: Offline hash records for recovery images and a verification log.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore from the protected copy and attest independently.

name: Destruction of ground backups and configuration
description: Delete or encrypt backups, configuration stores and virtual-machine templates before the main attack.
precondition: Backups are online and reachable with administrator rights.
detection: Backup-job failures, retention changes and deletion events.

assessment.question: Could one administrator account delete every copy of the mission database?
assessment.evidence: Evidence of offline or immutable backups and a restore test.
assessment.recovery_test: Restore the mission database from the offline copy within the target time.

name: Key and credential lockout of the operator
description: Change keys, counters or credentials so the legitimate operator can no longer authenticate to its own spacecraft or systems.
precondition: Rekey or credential-change functions can be used by the adversary.
detection: Rekey events without an approved ceremony; authentication failures from legitimate stations.

assessment.question: Is there a protected last-resort way to regain command if operational keys are changed against us?
assessment.evidence: Design and test evidence of a recovery key or path that normal operations cannot alter.
assessment.recovery_test: Regain command of the flatsat after operational keys are replaced.

name: Denial of alternate command paths
description: Jam, compromise or pre-empt the backup stations and networks the operator would turn to in a crisis.
precondition: Backup paths share providers, credentials, locations or frequencies with the primary.
detection: Health monitoring of backup paths; periodic live use.

assessment.question: What do the primary and backup command paths have in common?
assessment.evidence: A common-mode analysis of primary and alternate paths.
assessment.recovery_test: Command through the alternate path with the shared elements declared lost.

name: Interference with incident response
description: Watch responder communications, tamper with response tooling or feed false information to slow and misdirect the response.
precondition: Responders use the same systems the adversary already controls.
detection: Access to responder mailboxes and tickets; security tools being reconfigured.

assessment.question: Could we run an incident without using any system the intruder might control?
assessment.evidence: An out-of-band communications plan and evidence it has been used in an exercise.
assessment.recovery_test: Run one exercise entirely on out-of-band channels.

name: Re-entry through unrotated trust
description: Return after eviction using credentials, keys, tokens or vendor connections that were not changed during recovery.
precondition: Recovery restores service faster than it rotates secrets.
detection: Use of pre-incident credentials or keys after recovery.

assessment.question: After an incident, what is the complete list of secrets to rotate, including on orbit and at suppliers?
assessment.evidence: A rotation checklist with owners and a timed dry run.
assessment.recovery_test: Complete a full rotation in an exercise and verify old secrets fail everywhere.

name: Timing against critical operations
description: Strike during launch and early operations, manoeuvres, anomaly recovery or holidays, when margin and attention are lowest.
precondition: Critical periods are predictable and staffing or authority is reduced.
detection: Heightened monitoring during critical periods; intelligence warnings.

assessment.question: During our most delicate operation, who has authority to stop and switch to a safe configuration?
assessment.evidence: Go and no-go criteria that include security conditions for critical operations.
assessment.recovery_test: Inject a security event into a critical-operations rehearsal.

name: Common-mode defeat of redundancy
description: Defeat spares and redundant chains by exploiting what they share: identical software, keys, suppliers or management.
precondition: Redundancy was designed against random failure, not deliberate common cause.
detection: Simultaneous anomalies in primary and redundant units.

assessment.question: What single flaw is present in both the primary and the backup?
assessment.evidence: A common-cause analysis covering software, keys, suppliers and operations.
assessment.recovery_test: Operate with primary and identical backup both declared untrusted.

name: Erosion of assurance and attribution
description: Leave doubt: imitate natural anomalies, plant misleading traces or simply make it impossible to prove the system is clean.
precondition: The operator cannot independently attest spacecraft state or distinguish attack from fault.
detection: Anomaly investigation that always includes a security hypothesis.

assessment.question: After an anomaly, how would we prove to a customer that it was not an intrusion?
assessment.evidence: An anomaly procedure with a security branch and the evidence it collects.
assessment.recovery_test: Produce an attestation of spacecraft state from independent evidence in an exercise.
